feed.title: NPR Topics: Politics
feed.subtitle: Follow NPR Politics for nonpartisan coverage of government, elections, policy debates and voting rights. Plus weekday audio from The NPR Politics Podcast.

entry.title: The latest from Trump's press conference
entry.summary: President Trump gave a wide-ranging press conference following his historic trip to Asia where he met with Chinese President Xi and Russian President Putin.

entry.title: A second judge blocks Trump's arch, saying it's unlikely to succeed in court
entry.summary: A federal judge in Virginia said she will issue a preliminary injunction against Trump's arch, going a step further than the D.C. federal judge who temporarily blocked construction earlier this week.

entry.title: Trump initially accepted the midterm results, but most GOP voters doubt they were fair
entry.summary: Less than half of Republicans nationwide considered the midterm elections "free and fair," according to new polling.

entry.title: Trump touts meeting with Xi and Putin but offers little results
entry.summary: At a White House press conference Friday, Trump offered little in actual results of the meetings, beyond a joint statement on unity over some issues.

entry.title: Texas execution took over an hour as staff struggled to find vein; Reinaldo Dennes moaned about pain
entry.summary: The same day Dennes was given lethal injection, Florida carried out a record-breaking 20th execution of the year.

entry.title: Dems aim to block Iran war funding. And, Army delays lead azide detonation in Iowa
entry.summary: Congress needs to pass a funding measure to avoid a shutdown next month, providing Dems an opportunity to leverage power. And, the Army says waiting to detonate lead azide could become dangerous.

entry.title: GOP Sen. Johnson rejects tying government funding to an end to the Iran war
entry.summary: "We're not going to shut down the war," Sen. Ron Johnson said as Republicans and Democrats struggle to reach a government funding deal.

entry.title: Senate passes bipartisan energy bill amid environmental concerns
entry.summary: As Americans struggle with rising energy costs and increased demand driven by AI, the Senate passed a bipartisan bill that will speed up the approval process for data centers and power plants.

entry.title: New York City unveils a bold plan to move its jails off Rikers Island
entry.summary: New York City officials are moving forward with plans to close Rikers, the city's main jail complex, after years of discussion. The jail has been plagued by assaults and inmate deaths.

entry.title: Judges have put Trump's arch and golf course on hold, but only for a matter of days
entry.summary: A federal judge has twice delayed construction of Trump's arch. Another is keeping East Potomac Park open. The proposed golf course redesign got mixed feedback from a federal arts panel on Thursday.
